From the Supra Table

Traditional Georgian & Caucasus Dishes

A curated selection from a deep menu, each dish carrying the memory of a region, a season, and generations of the hands that shaped it.

Khinkali

Hand-pleated soup dumplings, twisted at the crown.

A mountain dish from Pshavi and Khevsureti, filled with spiced meat and broth. Held by the knot, bitten open, and never touched by a fork.

Khachapuri

Molten cheese cradled in a warm crust.

The Adjarian boat, crowned with egg and butter, sits beside the folded Imeruli round. Regional to its core, comforting on every table.

Lobio

Slow-stewed beans with coriander and walnut.

Simmered in a clay pot with blue fenugreek and marigold, served with hot mchadi cornbread. A humble dish carried across every Georgian region.

Pkhali

Cool vegetable pâtés bound with walnut.

Spinach, beet leaf and green beans pounded with garlic and spices, crowned with pomegranate. A cornerstone of the Georgian appetizer spread.

Churchkhela

Walnuts strung and dipped in thickened grape must.

The traditional Georgian sweet, hung to dry through the autumn harvest. Chewy, fruity, and older than any recipe book we could name.

Qvevri Wine

Amber wine fermented in buried clay.

Made the way it has been for eight thousand years, in egg-shaped vessels set into the earth. Poured freely, as any proper supra demands.
